title: Taking disjoint unions of semirepresentable hypercovers
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small subcanonical site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with fibre products, and fix $T\in\mathcal C$. Subcanonical means every representable presheaf $h_A=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(-,A)$ is a sheaf. Let $K$ be an augmented simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] of $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C/T)$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct], with $K_n=\{A_{n,i}\to T\}_{i\in I_n}$. Assume its degree-zero and proper-face matching arrows are componentwise covering families (over each target member the corresponding source arrows form a covering). Assume that $A_n=\coprod_{i\in I_n}A_{n,i}$ exists in $\mathcal C/T$ for every $n$, and that the canonical maps $\coprod_{i\in I_n}h_{A_{n,i}}\to h_{A_n}$ are isomorphisms of sheaves of sets on $\mathcal C$. Then taking disjoint unions of the component maps defines an augmented simplicial object $A_\bullet\to T$ of $\mathcal C$. Every matching arrow $h_{A_n}\to M_n(h_{A_\bullet}/h_T)$ is an epimorphism. Here $M_0=h_T$, and for $n>0$ the matching object is the finite limit of the compatible proper-face diagram in the category of sheaves of sets over $h_T$, so $M_1=h_{A_0}\times_{h_T}h_{A_0}$.

proof.text: For every simplicial operator between the families, take on each component the given map into the corresponding component and then use the coproduct universal property to obtain the map between A_n and A_m. The componentwise identity and composition equations imply the identity and composition equations for these maps, and the same construction handles the augmentation to T. Thus the maps form an augmented simplicial object A_\bullet\to T.

proof.text: Work over $T$. The slice $\mathcal C/T$ has terminal object $T\to T$ and fibre products, so [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits] and [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object] give the formal matching family $B_n=M_n(K)$ for every $n$, with $B_0=\{T\}$. For a family $Q=\{V_j\to T\}$ define the presheaf over $h_T$ by $F(Q)(U)=\coprod_j\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(U,V_j)$. This functor preserves finite limits in the slice: its terminal value is $h_T$, and the displayed fibre-product family of the finite-limits node gives, sectionwise, pairs $(j,u),(k,w)$ with equal target index and equal composites to that target object. This is precisely $F(Q)\times_{F(R)}F(Q')$. Finite products are pullbacks over the terminal object and equalizers are pullbacks along diagonals, so this checks all finite limits. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact], sheafifying the finite matching diagram gives the canonical projection-compatible isomorphism $F(B_n)^\#\cong M_n(F(K)^\#/h_T)$. Here $h_T^\#=h_T$ by subcanonicity, so the same finite-limit comparison applies over $h_T$.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq0$ and a section of $F(B_n)^\#$ over $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], a covering of $U$ makes it the image of sections of $F(B_n)$, each a pair $(j,u:U_a\to B_{n,j})$. Write the formal matching map as $(\alpha,(f_i)):K_n\to B_n$. Its covering hypothesis says that $\{f_i:A_{n,i}\to B_{n,j}\}_{\alpha(i)=j}$ covers $B_{n,j}$. Pulling this covering back along $u$ gives a covering $U_a\times_{B_{n,j}}A_{n,i}\to U_a$; the projections to $A_{n,i}$ are sections of $F(K_n)$ lifting $(j,u)$. The composition axiom for site coverings makes these successive covers a covering of $U$, and their lifts give lifts to $F(K_n)^\#$. Thus $F(K_n)^\#\to F(B_n)^\#$ is locally surjective and is an epimorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective]. This works also for $n=0$, where $B_0=\{T\}$.

proof.text: By the sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], $F(K_n)^\#$ is the coproduct of the representable sheaves $h_{A_{n,i}}$: maps from either object to a sheaf $H$ are exactly families of maps $h_{A_{n,i}}\to H$. Hence the assumed canonical isomorphisms give $\eta_n:F(K_n)^\#\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{A_n}$. They commute with each simplicial operator and the augmentation, since on the $i$th representable summand both composites are postcomposition by the component map followed by its coproduct inclusion, and those summands determine a map from the sheaf coproduct. For each $n$, compose the matching projections with the corresponding $\eta_m$ to obtain a cone; the matching universal property [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object] gives $\eta_{M_n}:M_n(F(K)^\#/h_T)\to M_n(h_{A_\bullet}/h_T)$. Repeating with $\eta_m^{-1}$ gives an inverse, because both composites have the identity on every limit projection. The square of matching arrows commutes: its composites with every face projection agree by the simplicial compatibility just checked. Combining Step 2 and Step 3, the bottom matching arrow is $\eta_{M_n}\circ\mu_n\circ\eta_n^{-1}$, where $\mu_n$ is an epimorphism. Cancellation in the definition of epimorphism therefore makes the bottom arrow an epimorphism. For $n=0$ the target is $h_T$ and the target identification is the identity; for $n=1$ the finite limit over $h_T$ is $h_{A_0}\times_{h_T}h_{A_0}$.
